title: Track Anthropic API costs per job
description:
Record token usage and estimated cost from the Claude API response for each processing job. Store in the DynamoDB job record and display a cost breakdown in the frontend.

## Implementation

### 1. generator.py — return usage alongside HTML
`stream.get_final_message()` is already called (line 40). The response object has `response.usage` with:
- `input_tokens` (int) — tokens consumed from the PDF + system prompt
- `output_tokens` (int) — tokens generated for the HTML output

Change `generate_html()` to return a tuple: `(html, usage_dict)` where usage_dict contains:
- `input_tokens` (int)
- `output_tokens` (int)

### 2. Pricing (Claude Opus 4.6, standard tier)
- Input: \$5.00 / million tokens
- Output: \$25.00 / million tokens

The SDK does NOT provide cost estimates — must calculate from tokens x price.

### 3. lambda_process.py — calculate costs and persist to DynamoDB
After `generate_html()` returns, calculate costs and write to the job record:
- `input_tokens` (int)
- `input_tokens_cost` (str, USD e.g. "0.0850")
- `output_tokens` (int)
- `output_tokens_cost` (str, USD e.g. "0.3500")
- `total_cost` (str, USD e.g. "0.4350")

Add these to the existing UpdateExpression that marks the job as complete.

### 4. lambda_status.py — return cost fields in status response
Ensure the status endpoint returns the new cost fields so the frontend can display them.

### 5. index.html — show cost breakdown in the frontend
After the gist link (in the success/complete state), display a cost breakdown:
- Input Tokens: 17,000 (\$0.09)
- Output Tokens: 14,000 (\$0.35)
- Total Cost: \$0.44

Style it to match the existing UI (muted text, compact layout).

### 6. Files to modify
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| backend/generator.py | Return (html, usage_dict) from generate_html() |
| backend/lambda_process.py | Capture usage, calculate costs, write 5 fields to DynamoDB |
| backend/lambda_status.py | Pass through cost fields in response |
| backend/static/index.html | Display cost breakdown below gist link |

### Notes
- No infrastructure changes needed (no new tables, parameters, or IAM permissions)
- Use named constants for pricing (not magic numbers) since pricing may change
- Cost values stored as strings to avoid DynamoDB Decimal precision issues

title: Enforce rate limit in Upload Lambda
description: Before invoking the Process Lambda, check the daily count against the configurable limit. Return a 429 with a clear message if the limit is reached.

title: Track daily processing count in DynamoDB
description: Add a counter mechanism in DynamoDB to track how many articles have been processed in the current 24-hour window. The Upload Lambda should check this before allowing a new job.

title: Add footer with copyright and website link
description: Add a footer to the frontend: 'Copyright 2026 Amroja, LLC' on the left, link to https://johndamask.com on the right. Replace the existing 'Powered by Claude' footer.

title: Show rate limit error in frontend
description: Handle 429 responses from the upload endpoint and display a user-friendly message that the daily limit has been reached.

title: Add configurable rate limit parameter to CloudFormation
description: Add a DailyProcessingLimit parameter to nowigetit.yaml (default 20). Pass it as an env var to the Upload Lambda so it can enforce the limit.

title: Add descriptions to Secrets Manager secrets
description: Add Description field to the nowigetit/anthropic-api-key and nowigetit/github-token secrets in deploy.sh so admins can see what each secret is for in the AWS console.

title: Add daily processing rate limit (epic)
description: Create a configurable daily rate limit for article processing. Default is 20 articles per 24-hour period. An admin should be able to easily change this number.
